source.title: Evidence for feature-specific error correction in LLMs
source.citation: Francisco Ferreira da Silva et al., 2026
source.authors: Francisco Ferreira da Silva; S. Heimersheim

record.file_problem: No material file problem; the text is a full paper.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures whether candidate feature directions are privileged under activation perturbations. It does not measure how many neuron poles have one or two identifiable jobs, test explanations on held-out activations, study the Inception examples, or test neuron-based attribution graphs.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results about feature-specific error correction and candidate feature directions, which are related to the claim’s subject but do not test any listed version. Rows below record those related measurements with versions ["none"]. Literature results cited in the paper are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures whether candidate residual-stream directions (contrastive, MELBO, SAE) are more perturbation-sensitive than their mixtures. It reports this as a superellipse exponent p. It never examines individual neurons or neuron poles. It does not count jobs per neuron, score explanations, study InceptionV1, or build neuron attribution graphs. Its results are offered as evidence for superposition and error correction in the residual stream. That is the view the essay disputes, but it is not measured on the neuron units any version names. So no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as paraphrased. The authors conclude that contrastive, MELBO and SAE directions are privileged (p≈2.2–2.4, a likely lower bound), consistent with superposition and error correction, while PCA and random baselines give p≈2. They note that plateaus admit alternative explanations, such as manifold projection or learned robustness, and that p>2 is necessary but not sufficient for a direction to be a feature.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses residual-stream perturbations and fits a superellipse exponent to downstream response; it does not use a neuron-pole explanation or held-out activation-scoring procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports robustness across perturbation and measurement layers, response metrics, thresholds, perturbation methods, activation sources, token positions, and model settings; contrastive-direction means across ablations are reported in the [2.24, 2.63] interval.

fits_no_version.finding: Contrastive (mean p 2.42), MELBO (2.21) and SAE-decoder (2.28) directions in Gemma-2-9B have p above 2. PCA, random-difference and random controls sit near 2. The contrastive result holds across six LLMs and many ablations (means 2.24–2.63). p falls toward 2 when directions are rotated away from the candidates, and does the same from ground-truth features in a toy denoising model (p 3–3.4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLM residual streams show feature-specific error correction: perturbation responses privilege candidate feature directions over their mixtures and over non-feature baselines. This is consistent with computation in superposition over directions rather than neurons.

record.problems: The paper notes that it lacks ground-truth feature directions in LLMs, so candidate directions may be imperfectly aligned; it also presents alternative interpretations of activation plateaus and says p > 2 is necessary but not sufficient for a direction to be a feature. The toy model differs substantially from LLMs. These limitations concern the paper's FSEC interpretation; it does not supply evidence on neuron-job shares or the listed explanation tests.
record.rows_left_out: Figure-only per-model and per-ablation numerical values in Figure 6 were not transcribed as separate rows because the text gives only aggregate ranges for those settings. Figure 9 reports fit-residual distributions, which are fit diagnostics rather than outcomes about the claim's versions.

untested.parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or shares by number of jobs.
Six LLMs are studied, but only for direction-perturbation exponents. No neuron interpretability shares are reported, and no MoE or trillion-scale models are included.
No InceptionV1, cat-and-car neuron, pose or recursive-generalization analysis. Superposition is argued for residual-stream directions, not neurons.
No interpretable-neuron shares by architecture, regularization or tool quality, and no vision models.
No neuron-based attribution graphs and no comparison with replacement models.
Does not test whether explanations from activating examples predict firing.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: Neither original source is cited. The relation is 'discusses' only in the loose sense that the paper argues for superposition, which is the claim's counter-position. Its unit of analysis is residual-stream directions, never MLP neurons, so it cannot bear on neuron-pole shares. R3 omits the pair count; the text says only that the top-33 SAE latents were used. Rows are otherwise accurate.

versions.untested_parts: Does not audit Qwen3-32B neuron poles or report shares of poles by number of jobs.
Tests candidate-direction perturbation responses in several LLMs, not the shares of interpretable neuron poles across models or scale, and not models up to trillions of parameters.
Does not study InceptionV1 or the cat-and-car neuron, pose, or recursive generalization.
Does not estimate interpretable-neuron shares by architecture, regularization, or tool quality, or study InceptionV1-sized vision models.
Does not build or evaluate neuron-based attribution graphs or compare them with replacement models.
Does not test whether explanations based on activating examples predict where neurons fire.
Does not score neuron explanations by simulating their activations on new text.
